description: Shared HTTP/JSON service-operation catalog. The receiving owner defines each operation's method, path, schemas, errors, authorization and idempotency. Lab 4 Grade 5: callers send every operation to the MESSAGE BROKER (moved from the Gateway's service route). The broker authenticates the caller with its own credential, enforces the operation's caller allowlist, chooses a target instance from Service Discovery (round robin, skipping instances whose circuit is open), replaces the credential with the target's credential, adds X-Service-Name and forwards the same path. This is request/reply routing; queue and topic delivery are later work. The Gateway remains the public entry point for players (publicBackendCredentials below).

transport.callerSends: POST|GET <BROKER_URL><path> with Authorization: Bearer <caller credential> and X-Trace-Id
transport.brokerForwards: the same method, path and query to one target instance chosen by round robin among the Discovery instances whose circuit admits traffic, with Authorization: Bearer <target credential>, X-Service-Name: <authenticated caller>, X-Trace-Id and Content-Type only
transport.loadBalancing: per target service, round robin over Discovery's fresh instance list (moved from the Gateway)
transport.circuitBreaker: per instance: 3 failures (5xx, timeout, unreachable) within 3.5x the operation timeout trip it; the instance is skipped until a cooldown elapses, then probed once (half-open), and is submitted for removal from Discovery (moved from the Gateway)
transport.failover: only a connection never established (refused or connect timeout) is retried, once, on another instance; replies, 5xx and timeouts are never retried by the broker
transport.credentials: Every caller and every target has its own secret of 32-256 visible ASCII characters. No universal service token, no Discovery-token reuse, no player JWT on service routes. Secrets live only in deployment environments, never in Git.
transport.noGenericForwarding: The broker routes only the operations listed here; any other /internal path is 404. No caller-chosen target URL.
transport.identity: Public REST: the Gateway sets X-Player-Id from the verified access-JWT subject and discards any client value. Service operations carry no player identity header; player ids are body fields that the receiving owner authorizes.
transport.trace: X-Trace-Id is preserved on every hop and echoed on every response.

budgetsMs.note: Membership budgets remain fixed. Generation/readiness and durable callbacks may declare explicit per-operation budgets; fit child calls inside parent deadlines. 'broker' is the message broker's budget; 'gateway' is kept for the deprecated Gateway service route while callers migrate.

brokerErrors.401 UNAUTHENTICATED: missing or unknown caller credential (player JWTs and target secrets are not caller credentials)
brokerErrors.403 CALLER_NOT_ALLOWED: authenticated caller is not on the operation allowlist
brokerErrors.404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND: method and path are not a catalog operation
brokerErrors.503 SERVICE_AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED | DISCOV: the broker or every target instance cannot serve
brokerErrors.504 TASK_TIMEOUT: the operation's broker budget was exceeded

transport.legacyGatewayRoute: Deprecated for service-to-service calls (Gateway #51). Until every caller has moved to BROKER_URL, the Gateway's authenticated service route may still route these operations with the same allowlists and budgetsMs.gateway. Moderation and Discord DMs call only the broker.

operations.retry: the caller's outbox may resend the identical stored body after an outage, a deadline or a restart
operations.semantics: The only score/penalty mutation. reason DECISION, APPEAL_REFUND or DECISION_VOID; a decision causes at most one change of each reason. Session must not score DecisionRecorded again. New changes require ACTIVE state and the stored MODERATOR. Retries are recognized after completion. Adjustment reasons change score/penalties only; recorded correctness is historical and is not inferred from a refund/void. Post-completion result changes are forbidden.

ownedInitializationProtocol.scope: New HTTP operation candidate, not a change to an already deployed broker transport. Receiving owners must review before consumers merge.
ownedInitializationProtocol.sessionBinding: payload.sessionId is required, immutable, included as the last length-prefixed event hash field. Envelopes without session binding are rejected by the new receivers.
ownedInitializationProtocol.deadline: 500 ms target budget; receipt fan-out parallel with 400 ms per HTTP call. Membership budgets unchanged.

receiverReconciliation.rulesBinding: Session persists eventId and uses shiftId=sessionId because one Session represents one shift.
receiverReconciliation.remainingGap: Credential initialization uses a different payload/hash/receipt protocol from Applicant/Record; do not alias those endpoints. Consumer context ports remain proposals until owners reconcile them.
